newsitem.title: USA: NU-KOTE NAMES COO PATRICK HOWARD CEO.
newsitem.headline: NU-KOTE NAMES COO PATRICK HOWARD CEO.

text.p: Nu-kote Holding Inc, reporting a loss for the first quarter ended June 27, Thursday said it named chief operating officer Patrick Howard chief executive.
Howard replaces David Brigante, who will remain chairman and will focus on strategic initiatives, a company spokeswoman said.

In other management changes, controller Anthony Schmeck and treasurer Steven DiPasquale will share the chief financial officer's responsibilities. They replace Daniel Kerrane, who left the company. The spokeswoman said she did know why Kerrane left.
The manufacturer of printer supplies posted a loss of $6.0 million, or $0.27 a share, in the first quarter ended June 27. This compared with a 1.8 million net, or $0.08 a share, in 1996 quarter.
Sales dropped to $79.7 million from $87.5 million over the same period. The company attributed the decline to lower sales in Europe, which dropped to $36.8 million from $44.9 million.
Nu-Kote said August 4 it secured $145 million in financing from its existing creditors to pay for restructuring.

"I will be focusing my full attention on the restructuring plan, including the rationalization of manufacturing operations, the elimination of unprofitable product categories, and the redirection of resources to the most profitable non-impact categories," Howard said.
The company said its selling, general and administrative expenses dropped to $14.7 million for the quarter from $17.4 million last year.
Nu-kote's stcok traded at 1-9/16 Thursday morning, up 1/16.
